stem: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was proclaimed in Paris on 10 December 1948. Which body proclaimed it?
hints: The Declaration is a United Nations (UN) document, meant for "all peoples and all nations". That rules out the body of only one country.
Recall the closing lines of the Preamble. They name the body that "Proclaims this Universal Declaration of Human Rights".
Cross out the Congress of the Philippines (it serves one country) and the court (the Declaration is not a court ruling). Of the two UN bodies left, pick the one named at the end of the Preamble.

solution.methodName: Recall the exact words of the provision

steps.action: Note what kind of document it is: a UN declaration, made as "a common standard of achievement for all peoples and all nations".
Cross out the Congress of the Philippines.
steps.why: Article VI, Section 1 of the 1987 Constitution gives Congress the legislative power of the Philippines only. The Declaration is for all nations.

steps.action: Recall the closing lines of the Preamble: "The General Assembly, Proclaims this Universal Declaration of Human Rights..."
steps.why: The UN's own page also says it was proclaimed by the General Assembly, through General Assembly resolution 217 A.

steps.action: The answer is the United Nations General Assembly.

trapNotes.The United Nations Security Council: The Preamble and the UN page both name the General Assembly, through General Assembly resolution 217 A. The Security Council did not proclaim it.
trapNotes.The Congress of the Philippines: Congress makes laws for the Philippines only. The Declaration is a UN document meant for "all peoples and all nations".
trapNotes.The International Court of Justice: The Declaration is not a court ruling. The Preamble says the General Assembly proclaimed it.

sourceRef.citation: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Preamble (UN General Assembly resolution 217 A)
